utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Issa, are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour. Thank you. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, just continuing on from yesterday, did you see any regular soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were soldiers, but it's been eight years since then. I don't know. There were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I was a regular soldier from 1993 to 1995, until the end of the war, an active-duty soldier. So of course there were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So just to be absolutely clear on what you're saying, there were soldiers that were not necessarily in the military police from the Bratunac Brigade in Potocari. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were. There were.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what were they doing there, those other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what they were doing. There was a war going on. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, what did you see them doing? What did you observe?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in the compound where the Muslims were. I don't remember all the details of what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were they interacting with the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They talked to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What else were they doing, aside from talking to them?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know why they were talking to them?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know what their duties were at the time?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know specifically. Probably the leaders of their units would know, but I really wouldn't know. I was just an ordinary soldier there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, did you ever overhear anything that they were saying to the Muslims, any of them?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really didn't hear anything. I wasn't interested in hearing. I really didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were there other Serb military forces in Potocari, aside from members of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were, there were. Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Around what time of day did the transportation of the Muslim refugees stop for the day, sir?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember because I went to Bratunac. The military police withdrew the section for Bratunac, the few military policemen who were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And around what time did the military police withdraw to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember now. It's been eight years since then. I can't remember all the details. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you give us an approximate time.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that day or in general?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I mean that day. Approximate time when you withdrew and went back to Bratunac. Was it in the evening or the afternoon --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Leading the witness. I don't want to be objecting, Your Honour, throughout the day, but I will. And I will be very aggressive with this particular Prosecutor if she continues to lead in the way she did yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe I was leading the witness yesterday. I think I'm at this point attempting to refresh the witness's memory by asking him the time of day in general. I'm not asking him for a specific time. I'm simply trying to find out whether it was during the daytime or the evening. And in my respectful submission that is completely proper to -- in an attempt to refresh the witness's memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In this context I don't think it's a leading question because the witness asked the Prosecutor, you mean that day or in general? Then the Prosecution asks: I mean that day, approximate time when you withdrew and went back to Bratunac. Was it in the evening or the afternoon? I don't think it's a leading question. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, can you answer that question, please.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been 4.00 or 5.00. I'm not sure. It was summertime. It's difficult for me to orient myself. We received the order to withdraw because the Muslims were in a school.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And we had to secure that school.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's talk about that then, the school. Which school was it that you're referring to that you had to secure?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the Vuk Karadzic primary school.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who was in that school?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims, the Muslims who were brought there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where were they brought from?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where they were brought from, but they were brought to that school. Potocari, Srebrenica, Konjevic Polje, Glogova, I really don't know. There were soldiers there. I don't know who was sent where, but they brought them to the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did they bring them to any other locations in Bratunac, aside from the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I explain it? There were hangars or warehouses. We called them hangars which the pupils used for their practical work, and they were brought there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And where were the hangars and the warehouses located in relation to the Vuk Karadzic school? How far away were they?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. 10 to 50 or 100 metres. I don't know, I didn't measure it. I wasn't interested, but it was in the school area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And how many Muslims were in the area, were detained in Bratunac that evening, approximately?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite a few. There were quite a few. I can't tell you the exact number. I don't know, but there were quite a few Muslims, quite a lot.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Can you give me an approximate number?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The numbers that people mention would say there were thousands of them, but I really wouldn't know. There were a lot.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And you've indicated that you and the military police provided security for them. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who ordered you, sir, to provide security at the school and these other places in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our commander, Mirko Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell me, sir, when you were providing security at the Vuk Karadzic school, were you inside or outside the school?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside the school, across the road. If I had a piece of paper, I would draw it for you to explain exactly where I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, if you'd like to do that, we can provide you with a piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can also explain it like this. It's all the same to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you see while you were there guarding the Muslims outside of the school?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the Muslims going in, being brought in by buses. That's what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslims being abused while you were there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for me, no, I didn't see anything like that, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you hear that Muslims had been abused?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There probably was abuse and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said it's possible that they were abused, but I wouldn't know why.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how many nights did you spend guarding people in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I can't remember the exact time. One, two, three days. Eight years have elapsed since the end of the war. I was there. I was providing security. I admit that, yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And the first night that you were providing security in Bratunac, when was that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the date, really.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, if --

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it was the 12th or the 13th, I can't be sure exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Going back, sir, to the 12th of July during the day when you were in Potocari, did you see any Muslims that you knew while you were in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw quite a lot of people, neighbours of mine, schoolmates, yes, I did. But there was nothing I could do to help them at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if we could go into private session very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslims being abused in any way in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I ask you a question, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, normally, sir, the way it works is my job is to ask you the questions and your job is to answer the questions. These are the rules of the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, if you cannot understand the question posed to you by the Prosecutor, you could ask a question to the Prosecutor to clarify it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I should have said -- added that, but I didn't. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you repeat your question. I'm a bit confused. I was going to say something.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see any Muslims being abused in any way?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really didn't see that. I'm saying everything I know. I'm not lying. I can speak in public any way you like.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you see men being taken across the road from the UN compound and detained in a white house?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it personally, but I heard stories about it. I heard that this happened, because General Ratko Mladic, as I heard, said: Don't shove. You'll all have your turn. There were lots of women and children and men there. And he said: Your turn will come. I heard those stories. I didn't see that myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Who did you see boarding the buses?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Women, children, elderly people. Men as well, some men. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you separate any men from their families, sir?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not, but those lies -- I can't remember her name again. That -- this woman -- I'm really not interested in that woman. Could you please repeat that woman's name?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, sir, in fairness to you, and I know which woman you're referring to, but we have some information that witnesses, and not just referring to one person, saw you separating men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could go into private session, she can name the witnesses or the witness can exit. I would like to know who these witnesses - plural - are who specifically state that this gentleman here was separating men and women. So if they can give us a -- I assume there's a good-faith basis for asking that question. I do know that the woman that was mentioned earlier has made that allegation. But as far as others I would like to know which names they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But to be fair to this witness, let's go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are now in private session. Ms. Issa, you may remind this witness of that woman's name.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay, sir, the witness was named Muniba Mujic. Do you recall the name now?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. This is the woman who told those lies, and she said that I had separated her brother. And I never did any harm to anybody. You can put me in front of any expert to see whether they can prove that I did that. I know that I have been a suspect of war crimes, but I never did any such thing. I never separated anybody, let alone kill somebody. These things are terrible lies, disgusting lies. I really don't know what to call these things. Maybe when I walked up to Medina to take her children, maybe somebody heard me saying something like: Please don't push, or let the children get on the bus. Maybe they misinterpreted my words. But in any case, these are lies. Maybe they just misinterpreted it and they thought that I was separating people. I never did anything bad to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I assume that we're going to be getting the names of all the others. Otherwise I would ask that that portion of the transcript be either struck, and I understand that there's no procedure for that, but I would ask that there would be a curative instruction to the Prosecutor that if she's going to be doing that, she needs to provide us those names. She just can't make allegations that people are saying that this gentleman was involved in separating. If there are names, we would like to know so we can then check them out. I'm not saying there is no good-faith basis. I certainly am unaware at this point in time. So if she does have some names, perhaps they could provide us the names. They don't have to do it in front of the witness, because I understand that may compromise the safety of those other witnesses. But we would like to know the names of those other witnesses. So, the first question is: Are there other names? Yes or no. If so, we would like to have them. I think it's fair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I do think that's fair, and I'm not -- I'm going to have to check that, because my information was there may have been one other person who made that statement. I'm not entirely sure at this point, but I will look over the break. And if I am mistaken, then I will obviously advise the Court. But I need some time to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But at least the Defence counsel is entitled to know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But it's not just that, Your Honour, it has a chilling effect. Because this is a technique used often in North America in order to smoke out a witness. And frankly it is improper when a lawyer poses a question to a witness they must have a good-faith basis for that. They can later on lay the foundation, or they can later on bring in the witness. But in order to -- when you pose such a question to a witness, you must have a good-faith basis. This is -- it's one thing to do it when you are interrogating or interviewing a witness where you're trying to elicit information; it's another thing to do it in front of the Court. Now obviously we are before Professional Judges and there lies a slight difference than in front of a jury where it would have some dramatic implications. But nonetheless, I would ask that if there are such -- first of all, that this technique never be repeated. She's had plenty of time to be prepared. I'm imposing --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, I'm going to interrupt at this point --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: By posing that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You're in front of the witness, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: By posing that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This needs to be discussed -- can we discuss this outside the presence of the witness. All these personal allegations, this is not necessary --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There are no personal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, do not argue with each other in this courtroom for the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There were -- there was plenty of time, Your Honour, for this particular Prosecutor to have that information before posing the question; that's all I'm saying. It's nothing personal. And I would appreciate it if Mr. McCloskey would refrain and use a little bit of self discipline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, the Prosecution has already promised you that they will check it out during the break. And before that, I think your allegation of using that kind of technique is not standing at this moment. Let's move on, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour, I will move on. I think we can actually -- I'm sorry, Your Honour. I think we can actually move into open session. If we can go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go back to open session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Blagojevic. Your microphone, please. Thank you. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, to have to say the following. But in the interest of justice, I would kindly ask you, let's not defer anything for later. Let things be said immediately here and now. Let's see what the OTP have. Let them be fair and honest in the presence of this witness. Let them say everything that they think can be in the interest of justice. I wanted to say a little while ago, but I did not see the right moment. The witness was already in. I wanted to say something. I will ask the floor. Later on I would like to say something about a procedural matter. What I would like to see happen here is that we go to the very end to look the truth in the eye. We cannot leave anything for later. Let us hear who these people are. Let this witness say what he has to say. Let's bring these things to an end. I want to leave this place clean and clear. Wherever I go, I want to be clean. I'm in a very specific situation with regard to the legality of my defence. The OTP is aware of that thing and Blagojevic is just one person, but the truth is universal. I want things to be clarified here without any speculations. Let's bring things to an end as they should be brought to an end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Blagojevic, I believe that your view has been fully expressed by your counsel. I don't think there is any differences between you. And as this Bench has already reminded you for many times that if you have any objections, please get in touch with your counsel and express your view to them. It is our belief that whatever is in your mind, so long as you have communication with your Defence counsel, will be expressed to us. The practice to express your dissatisfaction before the witness is not proper. You may ask the Bench to allow the witness to leave this courtroom in the future. Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can go into private session very briefly. I just have a couple of comments to make in relation to that issue. I am able to respond at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, let's go to private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, at some point, did you hear that Muslims had been executed?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your word "executed." What do you mean by executed?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us, sir, whether you heard any rumours as to what happened to the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that they were killed and the figure mentioned was something between 7.000 people who were either killed or gone missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And did you hear who killed them?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the army. I -- allegedly, the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you aware of any investigation into the killings by the Bosnian Serb army or the Bosnian Serb government, rather?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand. Can you please repeat. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you aware of any investigation into the killings by the Bosnian Serb government?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you aware of the reburial programme that took place in September or October of 1995?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you and members of your unit participate in the reburial programme?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we provided security for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Where did you provide security, what location?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bratunac, Potocari, Srebrenica, Divici towards Zeleni Jadar. That's where they were transported. That's what we were told that they were going up there. We were providing security for the road and security passage for the lorries to prevent any delays or breakdowns.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay and who gave you instructions to secure the road?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My commander, the commander of the military police ordered us to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And that's Mirko Jankovic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mirko Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you indicated that you were providing security to prevent the potential of the trucks or the lorries breaking down. Can you tell us where the trucks were coming from.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told that a burial site was being moved from Glogova, and that this had to be transferred from there. What do I know? That's what we were ordered in my command.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where were the bodies being taken to?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where, but that's the general direction to which they were taken. I don't know exactly. I was -- before the war, I was never in Zeleni Jadar. I don't even know where Zeleni Jadar is. I live 20 or 30 kilometres away from that place and I never went there. I never went towards Zeleni Jadar. I don't know where it is, but I was told that's where they were being taken to.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. How long did the reburial process take, sir?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how long, but there were works. Works were going on. I don't know exactly how long they took. I don't know how long the removal of this burial site lasted. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, can you -- was it one day or longer?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not done during the day. This was done in the evening or during the night, so we are talking nights rather than days. When we provided security, it was during night.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Who else was securing the road from the military police with you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean my colleagues who were there with me?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was eight years ago. I can maybe remember one or two people who were with me, but I can't say for a fact that they were really there with me. I should think that they were with me. Bosko Lazic is one of them, and I remember Milovan Mitrovic. It was a long time ago. It was eight years ago. It's hard to remember. It's really very hard for me to remember all of these people. I remember Bosko because we were rather close and we are still close to this very day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Can you describe the trucks that were transporting the bodies?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was dark. It was during the night. I couldn't see much. There was no light. I suppose that they were, what, military trucks, civilian trucks. I don't know. I can't remember. I didn't see them. The army used whatever, whatever was at hand. They used civilian vehicles, passenger vehicles, civilian trucks, all sorts of trucks. So I really can't remember. It was dark and I didn't see them in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you aware of bodies in and around the Vuk Karadzic school and the hangars on the 13th and 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were stories, and according to these stories, there were bodies. But I personally didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where were those bodies, according to the stories?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were there in the place that you have just mentioned, but personally I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Moving then on to another topic. When you were interviewed, sir, in Banja Luka on the 31st of October, 2002, you were shown some photographs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you were also shown a video clip depicting Potocari and another clip depicting Sandici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was shown that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to show you a photograph from Sandici, turning then to Exhibit 662.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher. If we can put that photograph on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recognise anybody in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated in Banja Luka that there had been a change. I said that this was Momir Nikolic and that I was also with him, next to him. However, this photo was taken in Sandici. That's what you are saying. I'm not in that photo because I was not in Sandici. I never moved anywhere from Bratunac. When things were happening in Srebrenica, I didn't go anywhere. I only went to Han Pijesak once, but I don't know when it was. If this is Potocari, then I may be in the photo, but I really am not clear on this photo because I wasn't there. And that's what I claim. I wasn't there. It is possible that this is Momir Nikolic, and that there are people who look like me. On my return from Banja Luka, I came to Mirko Jankovic after having finished my interview. I said to Mirko Jankovic: There is a photo, a photo from Sandici. And, Mirko, you know I never went there. And he says he was my commander. And he says: Well, Momir probably went there. I really don't know. And Mirko told Momir went. But I, personally, I didn't go. And he told me: Momir went there. And then I said: Mirko, you probably know where you sent your people. I know that I didn't go there. But as I said, there are people who look like me, and I can say that in public or any way you want me to say that. I really wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just for the record then, sir, for the sake of completeness, I also showed you a couple other photographs when you and I met the other day. Is that correct? You have to answer --

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Turning then to P663, the Madam Usher can assist. If we can please place that on the ELMO. Were you able to recognise this person, sir?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other day I said when we were talking about this photo that I can try. Isn't that true? Isn't that what I said?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, why don't you just tell us, sir, what you said or what you -- if you can recognise this person. I mean, it's not a requirement. I'm just asking you a question. Do you or do you not recognise him?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I do not recognise him. He does look a bit like Momir Nikolic, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe this is from his younger days, but I didn't know Momir Nikolic before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could be a younger Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Moving then to the next photograph, 664. Do you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Just one more photograph relating to another area. If we can then show P22. Do you recognise anybody in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know this first man. His brother was my colleague; that's how I know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So are you referring then to the first man in the photograph numbered 1?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, bearing number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him by sight, but I don't know his name. Hold on just a moment. Is his name Brano? I don't know. I know the person, but I don't know his name and I haven't seen him since the end of the war. And his brother was my colleague. He was also a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you say also a policeman, he was a member of the military police unit you were in. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what I'm saying, a military policeman.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you know what unit or what brigade this gentleman was attached to during the war?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose since he is in Bratunac, he is a member of the Bratunac Brigade. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recall the specific unit, sir?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I recall the unit?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I can't. I know the person, but I don't know the unit. I don't know that many people here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know his last name? You said his name was Brano. Does he have a last name?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brano or Branimir, I'm not sure and his last name is Ilic, because that's what my colleague's family name was, this guy who was also a member of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can just have the Court's indulgence for a moment, please. Thank you, Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Mr. Karnavas, are you prepared to begin your cross-examination or we may have a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Either way, Your Honour, I leave it up to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there is still 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may start.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before coming here to testify, when you met with the Prosecutor last week, did they give you an opportunity to read your statement, the one that you had given in Banja Luka on 31st October, 2002?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You were able to read it in your own language?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't read it because I had a headache after travelling, but I did read it later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So before coming here today, you have had an opportunity to review it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to start with the 12th of July, 1995. Okay. As I read your statement --

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As I read your statement, on that particular day you were asked to accompany or to provide security for Momir Nikolic when he went to Potocari that morning. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact dates, but I did escort Momir then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you were asked about the first day when everybody had been gathered in Potocari, and it was the first opportunity to go to Potocari. So do you know whether it was the 12th or the 13th that you went there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it couldn't have been either the 12th or the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Was General Mladic there on that particular day in Potocari when you got there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in your statement you indicated that Momir Nikolic had come to the military police office and you were there, and that's when he asked you to go with him to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember. Eight years have elapsed, but whether it was he or Mirko Jankovic who gave me the order, I can't remember. But I was told to go with him and I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Yesterday you indicated that you were by the fountain in the centre of Bratunac when Nikolic approached you and asked you to go with him. Do you recall that? That was only yesterday.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that yesterday, but I can't remember whether it was he or Mirko Jankovic who told me this. You understand? I can't remember who specifically issued the order. I did say that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But yesterday you said you were at the fountain, and a year ago you said you were at the Bratunac Brigade military police office when Momir Nikolic came and asked you to go with him to Potocari. So my question is: Which is the more correct version, the one you gave a year ago or the one yesterday or you're just not quite clear? Which one?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that I was standing by the fountain, but I don't know how to reply to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. In any event, you do go to Potocari with Momir Nikolic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who was driving, you, Momir Nikolic, or a driver?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there. Momir Nikolic was there. And there was another man, but I can't remember who he was. And I think that Momir Nikolic was driving, but I can't be sure because I said to Momir, chief - that's what I called him - I said, chief, do we dare go to Potocari, because there was a war on. And he said: Why are you afraid? Get into the car. And I had to go. I was a soldier and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you called him chief because he was your Komandir's chief. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so he was -- we would -- not only would you take orders from Jankovic, but also Nikolic would directly order you from time to time as well. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to respect every officer, and as a military policeman, I was issued direct orders by Mirko Jankovic or if he was not around, his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Or Momir Nikolic as well. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it was on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, that's what -- I'm trying to get you to just tell us what happened. And your mission, your function, on that particular morning in Potocari was to provide security for Momir Nikolic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it in providing security, you had to be within a particular distance to make sure that at least he was within your sight and somewhat within your sound range. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't hear what he was saying. He went to the UNPROFOR base. I couldn't go in there. So I couldn't hear what he was saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But nonetheless you could -- you had him within sight? You were there to provide him security. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I believe yesterday you indicated that you saw other members of the military police that seemed to be around Ratko Mladic, the General. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And they were there to provide security for the General. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what their orders were. I know what I was doing, and the commander knows what he told them to do and what their duty was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you don't know whether they were there to protect or to secure -- to provide security for the general from UNPROFOR and the Muslims or whether they were there to protect security for the Muslims and UNPROFOR from Mladic or anybody else?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was some 30 or so policemen in the military police platoon, 30 or 35. I don't know what their duty was. Someone was securing the command, others were at Potocari, others were near the school. Everybody knew what his own task was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So in other words, you don't know exactly what they were there for? Yes or no. It's very simple.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, while you were there you did see some folks, Muslims, that you recognised. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said women. I didn't say men. These women who had gone to school with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it by now it has come to your attention that one particular woman, in fact, has indicated that you separated her brother away from her. Correct? You've heard that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it it is your belief that that never occurred. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally can say - it doesn't have to be in private session; it can be in any kind of session you like - what she said -- how can I explain this? It's possible that she wanted to take revenge on me, to set me up. I really don't know. (Redacted) (Redacted). When I went to help her children, because she had gone to school with me, perhaps I said to them, don't push, wait a while, in order to make room. And what she understood was that I had taken her brother and, as she said, killed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But as far as -- so your testimony here today is that you never separated her brother from her or anyone else. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hurt anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you ever given any orders, sir, to separate anyone on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally, no. I wasn't -- nobody said to me: Djokic, you have to separate. I was there providing security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So Momir Nikolic was your commanding officer at that particular moment, your Komandir while you were there. Your chief never ordered you to do any separation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't give me such an order. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But at some point you were given an order to go back to Bratunac and to come back with a truck that was full of bread, and I believe it may have had some water as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was water, too, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where was that bread picked up at, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the command of the Bratunac Brigade, in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it that's what you did, you came back with the bread?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was part of your function when you returned with the bread to also assist in distributing the bread?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a war on. I had to help distribute the bread and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now you were -- I think he's -- I was going to go into another line of questioning, Your Honour, that will require us to be in private session, so I think this may be a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll resume at quarter to 11.00

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, if we could go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in open session. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, let's leave Potocari. As I understand it, after that for the next day or two or possibly three days you were assigned security duty at Vuk Karadzic school to be on the outside. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you provide security anywhere else during those days, other than Vuk Karadzic, you personally?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in front of the fountain. I don't know whether that was on that particular day, but I provided security in front of the school, in front of the base, in front of the Fontana Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall who directly gave you those orders?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My commander, who else? Mirko Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he personally come up to you and say, Mr. Djokic, you're going to be assigned to provide security here?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I reported to -- for work, I read my daily order. It didn't have to come straight from his mouth. I just had to read my daily orders written by either the commander or his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Djokic, do you personally -- these may be unimportant matters, unimportant details; to us, they're very important. When I ask you a question, there's a specific reason. Okay. So my question is --

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, my question is: Did your commander specifically come up to you and ask you to go someplace and provide security? Yes or no or I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. However, I suppose that it was my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, how do you know it wasn't Nikolic as opposed to Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I know both of them. I know Nikolic; I know Jankovic, don't I.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So my question is: Could it have been -- since you're not sure whether it was Jankovic, could it have been Nikolic that ordered you? Yes, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I'll repeat it again. Who -- my question was with respect to Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know for certain, do you know for certain, that it wasn't Nikolic that ordered you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I -- if it comes from his mouth, then he -- then that means that he ordered me. If it comes from Mirko Jankovic's mouth, then it is Mirko Jankovic's order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And my question is: Who gave you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think you asked this question again and again, and the witness has already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: He said, he cannot remember whether it's Mr. Nikolic or Mr. Jankovic. I think it's very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated you did not leave Bratunac those days?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not that I didn't leave. I once went to Han Pijesak escorting some trucks. I don't remember what day that was, because it was eight years ago. But during that relevant period, I didn't go anywhere. When this transport of Muslims happened, I didn't go anywhere. I did go to Han Pijesak escorting some trucks. I was told to get on a truck and go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall who specifically, who specifically, directed you to get on the truck? And I'm not asking you to speculate, to guess, to surmise.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't intend to speculate. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, with respect to -- you were asked a series of questions about the reburial process. Do you recall those questions?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And your testimony was that you were ordered to provide security on the road. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the road, providing security for the trucks to prevent any obstacles on the road and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall the month of the year, sir?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact month, but it was two or three months later. I can't give you any details. I can't remember. I was there, but I can't remember exactly when that was. I remember the period of time when that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, again with respect to those orders, do you know for certain who it was that directed you to go out there during those nights and secure the road? And again, I'm not asking you to speculate. I'm asking you if you know for certain who ordered you.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that would be Mirko Jankovic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you recall Mirko Jankovic coming up to you and asking you specifically to go there and provide security on the road. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't personally say: Djokic, you go. This is how it happens: You come to work to the police station. We work in shifts. You would work two days and then you would be one day off. Or you would work three days and be one day off. I don't know how else to put it. So when you come to work it says somewhere, so-and-so goes to a certain place. So you get your tasks in the morning as you report for work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, in getting your task that I assume from listening to your answer was in writing, were you also given any verbal tasks along with that, or verbal clarification as to your task?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't get anything in writing. All of our tasks were given verbally. They tell you where to go. If he's not there, if the commander or his deputy are not there, then it's written and you go to a place where you find a list of your daily orders, daily tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's what I'm trying to get at, sir. Do you recall for certain whether you were given an oral task or whether you showed up and you found your name on a list where you were asked to report to, if you recall? If you don't recall, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So if you can't remember, when you said earlier that it was Jankovic that told you directly --

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- I really don't understand your question, sir. I don't know what you're getting at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. What I'm trying --

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the orders that I received came from Mirko Jankovic. I was a military policeman. All of my -- either verbal or written orders were from Mirko Jankovic. That's who I received them from. He was my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Do you recall, sir, do you recall whether you got an oral order or whether it was a written order to perform the security task on the road during this reburial process?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. It was eight years ago. I can't remember whether the order was verbal or written. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In getting that order to go and secure the road, were you told in advance what would be happening, or the purpose for securing the road?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were told that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you were told in advance that they would be bringing bodies in trucks and that you were supposed to protect the -- secure the road. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So it wasn't something that you just showed up on the road and all of a sudden you learned that that was what was happening?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko Jankovic held a meeting at which he told us that he had received an order from Momir Nikolic about reburial. And in that order, Momir Nikolic asked him to get his people ready. And then Mirko Jankovic ordered us to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, any cross-examination, Ms. Sinatra?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We have no questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any redirect, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do have a couple of questions. It won't be very long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honour, we can go into private session very briefly for these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Today you stated that you were ordered to provide security during the burial operation, reburial operation. What was your task in providing security?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we provided security for the road, preventing breakdowns, preventing stoppages on the road, to provide free passage for the lorries. That's what we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Were you ordered to prevent access to the burial sites by civilians or journalists?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't receive any such order. The only thing they told us was to move women and children away, because of the stench of those bodies. So we moved the children away so that children didn't see what we were transporting so that they wouldn't be traumatised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: You're referring to children and women. What women? What children?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb children and women, because the road goes through a settled area. It is a village, populated area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: So you were ordered to remove the civilian population from this village or villages during the burial process?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: You just stated that you were ordered to -- you stated, so you move the children away so the children didn't see what you were transporting.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To keep them away from the road, these children, so they -- because this is not just a village, it's a town. There was no way for me to move everybody from Bratunac and Potocari. It's a proper town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge's questions? Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, thank you Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: No, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage are there any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I would be seeking to tender numbers P663 through 665, those are the photographs. And I understand the photograph I referred to in the end, P22, was already admitted. Sorry, I'm just being handed a message here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, would you please identify the number again, because from the list I don't have the number 665.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. I've just actually realised what the problem was, Your Honour. These numbers were changed and I was looking at an old list. Perhaps I can just review it again. P662 was the photograph that I showed the witness of Sandici meadow. P663 was the photograph of the other individual that the witness indicated looks like Momir Nikolic. And P664 was identified by the witness as a photograph of Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any objections? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Those three documents are admitted into the evidence. Are there any documents to tender on the Defence side? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there was the one statement that I did show the witness, and of course the Prosecutor also asked some questions with respect to that. And that was identified as D88. I should note that this witness who is a protected witness under P-187, as I understand, has been moved by the Prosecution to come under 92 bis, unless I'm mistaken. So I would request at this point in time that in light of the questioning that the statement itself, if it hasn't come in already under 92 bis, that it be admitted as D88. So that would be our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we need assistance from the Prosecution to tell us whether they are admitted into the 92 bis or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: One more point of clarification, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let me hear the Prosecution, first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do believe that we moved to have that statement admitted pursuant to 92 bis, and we're just checking right now to see whether or not, in fact, it has been admitted. So momentarily I will be able to tell Your Honour, but we certainly did seek to have it admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I can clarify also. I have here a -- the -- their motion or their notice where it indicates that the Trial Chamber has reserved ruling on whether the witness will be called for cross-examination. So that was the point that I failed to mention, Your Honour. That could be found on page 22 of the 4 November 2003 Prosecution motion -- notice for filing of revised witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you going to call this witness to be a live witness to testify here? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, as you know, there's a few of these witnesses that are in -- sort of in this 92 bis category that I think the Court has reserved ruling, and we were, of course, seeing how this process turns out in order to help us all make the best decision possible. And I think we just need to think about where we go with these other witnesses in that regard. I don't think we made a decision yet. And I -- we're not sure whether these particular witnesses have been entered into 92 bis. I think Mr. Karnavas is right that it's still up in the air, but you can see there's factors we need to take into account because there's some important issues here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Well, I believe that if this witness is going to come to this Tribunal to give testimony, so this piece of document is not admitted into the evidence. But if he's not going to testify live in this Tribunal, this piece of the document will be admitted into the evidence, either through 92 bis or by the Defence counsel or we may have a double number on this piece of the document if it's all right with the parties. And this document I was reminded will be under seal. So at this stage, we do not make any rulings concerning this document, depends on the further decision by the parties, whether to call this witness live to testify. Yes, Witness. Thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. The usher will show you out of the room, and we all wish you a pleasant journey back home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good-bye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We were able to see what I believe was a ruling on that one witness. And I believe the Court has reserved its ruling -- the ruling says that you have allowed the statement under 92 bis, but you have reserved your ruling on whether or not we would be required to bring the witness for cross-examination. So we would, of course, like to hear your viewpoint on that, if you feel a need for this witness to come in. My guess is the witness would say the same thing she said in the statement. But if you want to see her say that and test the credibility of the witness, we can certainly have that witness brought in. And I haven't spoken to Mr. Karnavas what he would prefer also, and that's something that we try to consult with on these sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I -- thank you, Your Honour. Well, I do appreciate Mr. McCloskey's inquiry into what the Court would like to do. I think at this moment - and I haven't thought it through yet - but at this moment, I think I would agree with Mr. McCloskey that the witness in all likelihood is going to more or less say what she said in her statement. Obviously, there is some conflicting information, and I think that if we're going to be saving time and money that it would not be our position for this witness to be coming in, assuming that her statement does come in. And I think the record -- we've made a pretty good record at this point. So that would be my position, that it would not be necessary, though I'm always ready to cross-examine a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In light of the views expressed by the parties, we believe that we do not have to call this witness to be a live witness. So the statement will be admitted into the evidence at this stage, either as 92 bis or as the Defence evidence with the double number and under the seal. It is so decided. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. This is one of the witnesses where we had not yet gone through the Registry process of -- required under 92 bis where the Registrar -- oh, I'm sorry, we have. I'm sorry. It can go in under 92 bis. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, how about the next witness. Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The next witness should be just outside I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No protective measures for Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you please state your name for the record and spell your last name, please.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: My name is Pero Petrovic. I was born on the 8th of March, 1960, in Gornja Pilica in Zvornik Municipality. My father's name is Pajo and my mother's name is Cvijeta.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. And what is your current occupation, sir?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: Assistant warehouse keeper in Birac, in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And I understand, sir, that your ethnic background is Serbian. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you indicate what your occupation was or what you were doing during the war.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: During the war, the factory was not operating, and I was mobilised into the Army of Republika Srpska from the 20th of May, 1992. I was also the president of the Pilica local commune.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: I volunteered for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And can you explain to us what the Pilica local commune is.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: The Pilica local commune is an organ representing the needs of the population for the construction of infrastructure before the organs of Zvornik municipality. It is the local self government of the people in the area in relation to infrastructure, roads, water, electricity, utilities, everything that the local community needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And can you explain to us what was your role in the army. First of all, what unit were you attached to?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: I was in an infantry battalion which belonged to the Zvornik Brigade. The names of the battalions changed very often, but I played a very small part in the army. The battalion command was activated only in exceptional circumstances. We often worked together, and the battalion command would approve certain things for me in connection with roads and other things for the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And how long were you attached to that particular battalion?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: From the 12th of May to the 15th of March, 1996. I was on the list of the Army of Republika Srpska, I was mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who was your commander at the time, sir?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: The battalion commanders changed often. I could list them: Mihajlo Galic, Stevo Petrovic, Milan Stanojevic, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you were working, or when you were attached to the army, sir, were you directly active in the army most of the time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. How do you mean active?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you spend a lot of time on the front lines?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Very little time. I was in the rear more often in cooperation with the battalion command about the needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Can you elaborate on that. Can you explain to us why you were -- you didn't spend that much time on the front lines?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: My situation at home, because I was living on my own. My parents died in 1992, and the command of the Zvornik Brigade had understanding for me because of the needs of the household and the needs of the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Were you getting paid by the army during this period?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: I have to explain to you that I was on the payroll. There was a huge inflation, and the salary did not arrive on time. By the time it arrived, it was worthless, and that was at the beginning. And by 1995, there were no funds left.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what was your relationship with the commanders of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, it depends. It differed from moment to moment. In some cases, the battalion commander did not agree with me and sometimes I did not agree with him. The battalion commanders often reacted when I could not respond to their summons on time, so that this cooperation was sometimes tense.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have a particular issue with one commander?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. You mean problems -- the problems were trivial. How can I explain it? There was a number of cases when a soldier needed help and I would send them to the command for the army to help them or their parents. And -- because the soldiers were local people, most of them in that unit of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Were there times when you didn't obey the commander because of these problems relating to the local commune that you just told us about?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you ever disobey an order, sir, because of the problems that you just told us about in relation to the local commune?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: The local commune is an organ separate from the army, and the orders I received from the battalion command related only to my duties that had to do with the military.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Is there -- was there a time that you disobeyed an order?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. If the battalion command was looking for me, I would be a few hours late. And then I would be questioned as to why I had arrived late.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And why was that? Why would you arrive late?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: For example, because of my duties in the local commune, and sometimes because of my duties at home. If the commander sends you a courier telling you to report at 10.00 or 11.00 and you don't manage to arrive at that time on that day, then of course the commander would ask me why I hadn't arrived on time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Did you spend more time working for the local commune or more time working for the army during those days?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: I spent the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the number, the percentage of time he spent in the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, please, sir, so the interpreters can interpret that, please.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: I spent 90 per cent of my time working in the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, sir, in July of 1995, were you still working as president of the local commune in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And were you attached to a -- were you working in the military at that time? Were you active?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And around St. Peter's Day, sir, were you active in the military at that time or were you on leave?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: I was on duty, and in that period, I was to be deployed on the Nisici plateau, but they sent me home for 15 days instead because of the situation at home. So I was relieved of that period of 15 days that I was to spend on the Nisici plateau. So that practically I was free as far as the army was concerned, as far as the military was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us a little bit about the reasons behind that, what do you mean by the situation at home?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: I've already said that as of 1992, I lived on my own in our family house. My brother had been mobilised, and on the 30th of May there was a family tragedy in my close family. And probably this was why they gave me leave during those 15 days.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And were you ill around that time at all?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't feel so well after this tragedy in my close family. I can only remember that a day or two before I was going to go to the Nisici plateau, I had an inflamed tooth. And I had to go and see the dentist.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, in and around St. Peter's Day - and I appreciate you may not remember the precise date - can you describe what happened in and around that day on a particular day that was memorable to you.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC
utterances.text: A day before or on St. Peter's Day itself, one of my fellow villagers came to see me. And they were asking to be relieved of work duty because this person had a combine harvester. And I had forgotten to put him on the list of people harvesting wheat. And people who had combine harvesters were relieved of military duty during the time of the wheat harvest. Then I went to my office in order to ring up the commission of the Zvornik municipality, which was in charge of the harvest, monitoring the harvest, and the Kula -- at the Kula school, I ran into a woman who said to me: Pero, do you know what's happening? I didn't know. I couldn't explain to her what was going on, and she was unable to give me the details. So I asked a soldier what was going on. And they said that they had been informed by the brigade command that prisoners were to arrive. Should I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
